newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide to make $20 mln U.S. housing investment.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide to make $20 mln U.S. housing investment.

text.p: Nationwide Mutual said it will invest $20 million with two non-profit housing groups to help meet the housing needs of low-income renters and home buyers in the United States.
The investment will be administered by the Neighborhood Housing Services of America and the National Equity Fund, which will receive $10 million apiece.
Nationwide said its $10 million investment with Neighborhood Housing represents an increase over an earlier agreement to invest $3 million with the group.
Nationwide, the sixth largest homeowners insurer in the U.S., said its agreement with National Equity represents a separate, new investment.

The $20 million investment is in addition to the $13.2 million in grants the company is offering in connection with its U.S. Justice Department settlement of allegations that it discriminated against minorities in the marketing of homeowners insurance.

"Our investment will provide additional capital for more affordable residential mortgages in urban communities and assist with the rehabilitation of urban apartment complexes," Nationwide Mutual president Richard Crabtree said.
The National Equity Fund said it is a nonprofit syndicator of federal low income housing tax credits.

Neighborhood Housing said it plays a p ivotal role in providing financial liquidity to NeighborWorks organizations by providing a secondary market for loans that can not be sold on national, conventional or secondary mortgage markets.
